origin: Prior acting agent, copied without new robotics strategies
agent_conclusion: For the current microwave only: fresh-measure the handle/panel, plan grasp, approach with open fingers, physically close to observed contact, plan fresh relative refined arcs, inspect after each, and require task_success. The 8-step/no-tracking/20-degree candidate succeeded twice at 278 steps but failed to repeat on attempt15; its reliability remains uncertain.
agent_remaining_tradeoffs: Fewer closure steps and fewer tracking calls reduced control/tool calls in some episodes, but small closure changes affect contact and omitted tracking leaves late articulation-model questions unresolved. Arc plans can become unavailable after visible motion. The 8-step candidate is efficient when successful but not guaranteed.
scope: Repeated success in the same development scene; not transfer evidence.
representation: Historical evidence links removed. Tested relative control choices retained. No historical image regions, world poses, trajectories or raw replies supplied.

principles.principle: For an articulated door with a visible functional handle, fit current RGB-D geometry and make a fresh grasp plan, approach with open fingers, physically close, then use relative hinge arcs while checking each fresh view.
principles.applicability: Current visible rigid door, observable handle and cabinet-connected hinge, and planner support for a relative revolute arc. Must reobserve the geometry/contact in each scene; does not assume prior coordinates or pose transfer.
principles.procedure: Inspect multiple views and RGB-D; ground the handle/panel and compare the fitted direction with visible cabinet/handle layout. Plan grasp from current geometry; execute approach with open fingers; close and inspect jaw qpos/contact. Plan and execute one arc at a time, inspecting each resulting image. Official task_success supports benchmark completion; visible progress alone does not.

failure_modes.symptom: Grounding reports the handle is not on the opposite observed face despite visible apparent layout.
failure_modes.distinguishing_evidence: Compare current views, fit residuals and point cloud. In this scene the face diagnostic stayed false despite consistent visual arrangement; cause unresolved.

principles.evidence: Attempts1-13 each received official task_success=true, with later 20-degree/no-tracking versions successful in multiple resets. Attempts14-15 showed partial motion but task_success=false and late planner failures. Current-session observations and tool errors are cited in per-attempt findings; inherited successful-method.json was the starting procedure.
principles.reobserve: At every reset, inspect closed door, handle and cabinet relationship, fresh panel/handle depth, grasp qpos after closure, panel-to-cabinet movement and handle-to-gripper contact after each trajectory, plus returned success flag.
principles.transfer_test: Test on a fresh scene with a changed hinge side or handle placement and the same broad door mechanism. Falsified if the fitted geometry/direction fails to predict observed opening or if partial motion is misclassified as success.
principles.attribution: Inherited successful-method.json and tool documentation, refined with own current-scene observations.

principles.principle: Treat closure duration as an observed contact decision, not a fixed instruction; a visibly underclosed gripper can fail to transmit force, while a successful setting still needs fresh-reset confirmation.
principles.applicability: Physical parallel-jaw closure on an observed rigid handle; requires accessible jaw-position feedback and post-close view. Exact step counts/qpos are specific to this development scene and not transfer instructions.
principles.procedure: Close physically after the approach and inspect qpos and visual finger/handle relationship. If obviously underclosed, avoid applying a pulling arc until contact is improved. After choosing a setting, judge it by observed object motion and official result, then repeat from reset to support reliability.

failure_modes.symptom: Jaws remain more open and panel does not receive reliable motion.
failure_modes.distinguishing_evidence: Jaw qpos and visible engagement; attempt11's 5-step setting remained visibly underclosed and needed a 5-step recovery.

principles.evidence: 5-step attempt11 underclosed; 10-step attempts9/10 succeeded; 8-step attempts12/13 succeeded at 278 steps and attempt15 matched qpos but stalled. 7-step attempt14 showed visible motion but no success. Therefore no universal minimum closure is established.
principles.reobserve: Fresh handle diameter/orientation, jaw qpos before/after closure, finger placement, and whether the handle/panel moves with the gripper.
principles.transfer_test: Change handle diameter/material or grasp height and compare qpos plus observed force transmission. Falsified if the prescribed contact observation does not predict coupled motion.
principles.attribution: Own finding from current session; gripper/observation tool behavior inherited from tools.txt.

principles.principle: A method is repeatable only when fresh-reset episodes reach the official success signal; record visible progress, planner failures and success as separate evidence.
principles.applicability: Resettable simulator interaction with per-execution task_success and fresh camera observations.
principles.procedure: For each reset, state the hypothesis before motion; save plan; record fresh geometry; inspect after each trajectory; preserve exact failure messages and qpos; finish incomplete/uncertain when no feasible action remains. Compare repeated episodes and avoid promoting a partial success.

failure_modes.symptom: Same method succeeds in two trials but stalls in a later fresh reset.
failure_modes.distinguishing_evidence: Compare fresh measured qpos, command counts, images and plan errors. Attempts12/13 succeeded; attempt15 matched closure qpos but stalled later.

candidate_responses.response: Preserve successful procedure and test on next reset

principles.evidence: Thirteen official successes and two incomplete episodes. Attempts12/13 were repeated successes; attempts14/15 provide direct counterexamples to stronger reliability claims. No transfer test occurred.
principles.reobserve: Reset scene state, target geometry, contact state, per-trajectory views and official success booleans.
principles.transfer_test: Repeat on a different resettable articulated-object scene and then a different mechanism. Falsified if a claimed general method lacks fresh observable support or counts partial motion as success.
principles.attribution: Own session record plus supplied simulator success protocol.
